messages:
Alex: Heads-up — thinking about adding a dynamic preemption penalty + backoff layer to the dedicated GPU autoscaler. Goal: reduce noisy preempts for bursty tenants while keeping fast burst recovery. Thoughts?

Maya: Quick Q — are we penalizing tenants that caused the preempt, or the tenant that got preempted? we need to be clear in the model.

Alex: Good call. We should penalize the tenant that triggered preemption (the aggressor) so we don't punish victims. But also provide victims with emergency credits for short windows.

Sree: Draft idea: a hybrid "credit + penalty" model. Each tenant has a preempt_credit (0..100). When you preempt someone, you consume credit proportional to the eviction size. If credit < threshold, apply a soft penalty multiplier on admission (makes burst slower). Credits decay back on a long half-life. Simple formula sketch: 

```
# pseudo
penalty = base_penalty
penalty += preemptions_last_1h * 0.5
penalty += sla_violations * 2
penalty *= (1 + burst_size/100)
# apply penalty as admission backoff multiplier
admit_rate = base_rate / (1 + penalty)
```

Sree: Decay example: credit_replenish = min(100, credit + 1 per 6h) so full replenishment ~25 days. That prevents sustained bursters from cycling.

Maya: I like credit system for operator mental model. Two things to check: 1) fairness for enterprise tenants on contracts (SLA exceptions), 2) bounded latency impact (need SLO budget accounting).

Jordan: For rollout, we should simulate on historical traces first. We can run a sim with 30-day traces and compute change in 99p latency and preempt count. If sims look good, can canary in cluster with 5% traffic using a read-only admission shim.

Dina: Operator complexity warning — if credits live in operator/allocator state and are tuned by multiple controllers, debugging will be hard. Suggest exposing a simple /debug endpoint and a per-tenant history (last 7 days) so SEs can explain to customers. Also prefer server-side defaults and avoid per-tenant knobs initially.

Kevin: Billing/team ask: we need telemetry mapping from preempt_credit consumption -> cost bucket. If we throttle a tenant (penalty applied) we should emit events: `penalty_applied`, `credit_consumed`, `credit_replenished` with counts. That ties into chargebacks and support tickets.

Alex: Agreement: prototype credit system + optional penalty multiplier. Implementation pieces: credit ledger (persisted), admission path hook, telemetry + events, sim harness.

Sree: Minor note on ledger design — prefer append-only ledger backed by existing metastore (postgres). Keep tenant id, change_type, delta, reason, trace_id. That makes audits easy.

Maya: For SLA tenants we should have an override flag that requires a manual entitlements check (not automatic). Auto-overrides are dangerous.

Jordan: Experiment plan (short):
- run sim on 30d traces (owner: Jordan)
- small canary with `admission=soft` (no actual eviction) to collect signal (owner: Alex)
- full canary (10% traffic) with real credit consumption but doubled backoff windows (owner: Sree)

Dina: Add operator playbook entries: explain how to inspect ledger, how to reset credit in emergencies, and how to interpret debug endpoints.

Kevin: I'll add telemetry dashboards and an alert if a single tenant consumes >50 credits/day. Also add a billing tag for consumed credits (for internal showback).

deploy-bot: created canary job `sim/preempt-penalty-2026-03-01` -> https://ci.redwood/sim/2378 :pipeline_started :white_check_mark:

Alex: Decision (for now): implement credit + penalty prototype behind a feature flag. Default policy: conservative (slow replenishment, soft penalties). We'll iterate after sims.

Maya: SGTM :thumbsup:

Sree: I'll draft an RFC followup with formulas, API surface for ledger + events, and expected telemetry metrics (preempt_count, credit_delta, admit_delay_ms).

Jordan: I'll start the sim job and post results in this thread when ready.

Dina: I'll draft the operator playbook and admin endpoints design.

Kevin: Will wire dashboards and alerts.

Alex: Thanks all — keeping thread here for followups. If anyone wants to be added to the canary, ping me.
